extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges, marketplace administrators, policy stakeholders (agents/brokers), and public commenters on ACA eligibility rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory changes to Exchange failure-to-file-and-reconcile (FTR) processes, consumer noticing, income data-matching (DMI) procedures, and related verification/extension rules under the ACA for advance premium tax credit (APTC) and cost-sharing reductions (CSRs).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-tax year FTR process (reinstate pre-PHE policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstate the FTR process that requires Exchanges to determine enrollees ineligible for APTC when HHS notifies the Exchange that a taxpayer has failed to file a Federal income tax return and reconcile their past APTC for a year for which their tax data would be utilized to verify their eligibility (i.e., after one tax year of FTR status rather than two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: a one-tax year FTR acts as a backstop to prevent improperly enrolled enrollees from remaining enrolled and accumulating tax liabilities; implementation proposed beginning with OEP 2026 (fall 2025). Example/comparison: under one-tax year FTR, people receive notice they would lose eligibility unless they file and reconcile; under two-tax year FTR, they are not notified of imminent risk until after two years. Seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTR notice procedures: direct and indirect notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges may send (1) a direct notice to tax filers, (2) an indirect notice to enrollees, or (3) both; proposed reinstatement of pre-existing notice procedures that provide a series of notices beginning with two notices before OEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect notice included in Marketplace Open Enrollment Notice, available in online account and to Exchange call center, and educates enrollees on filing/reconciling requirements. Direct notice mailed via U.S. mail directly to the tax filer (not available online or to call center) to protect Federal Tax Information (FTI) and unambiguously explain failure to meet filing/reconciling requirements. IRS data rechecked in December; enrollees may attest; recheck notices sent; final recheck in spring leads to termination of APTC for noncompliant households. Seeks comment on reinstatement and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming change to §155.305(f)(4) notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise §155.305(f)(4)(i) and remove §155.305(f)(4)(ii) to align notice requirements with a one-tax year FTR process (rather than the two-consecutive tax year process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: prior Payment Notices expanded notice requirements for one- and two-year FTR statuses; because the proposal would require ineligibility after one year, the notice requirement aimed at two-tax year FTR no longer applies. The rule invites comment on the proposed conforming changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recheck / attestation / discontinuation safeguards for attesters
rubrics_metrics.description: If enrollees attest to having filed and reconciled, Exchanges will recheck IRS data multiple times; enrollees would be discontinued from APTC only after the IRS checks and rechecks their FTR status four times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: give ample notice to enrollees who may be confused and allow IRS processing time; process includes a final 'FTR Recheck' indirect notice to household contact and direct FTR Recheck mailed to tax filer warning of final loss of APTC absent compliance. Exchanges perform additional rechecks in the new coverage year to confirm attestations; then terminate APTC in spring for households still flagged by IRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges: flexibility in notice methods and alignment question
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges would be responsible for administering their own notice procedures with flexibility to send either direct notices containing FTI, indirect notices without protected FTI, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal seeks comment on whether State Exchanges should be required to align with Federal platform Exchanges on consumer noticing and recheck processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove automatic 60-day extension (§155.315(f)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.315(f)(7), which required Exchanges to provide an automatic 60-day extension in addition to the 90 days provided by §155.315(f)(2)(ii) for applicants to provide documentation to verify household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory/legal rationale: section 1411(e)(4)(A) and 1411(c)(4)(B) limit authority to extend the 90-day period; automatic 60-day extension viewed as outside statutory authority. Empirical rationale: post-implementation review shows the automatic 60-day extension did not meaningfully improve outcomes, increased APTC expenditures (estimated $170 million in 2024), and weakened program integrity. Ad hoc extensions under §155.315(f)(3) for demonstrated good faith will remain available. Seeks comment and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory interpretation limiting extensions of 90-day response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1411(e)(4)(A) allows HHS to extend the 90-day period for enrollments occurring during 2014 only; section 1411(c)(4)(B) limits modifications to methods for verification and does not authorize extending the 90-day response period generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Congress expressly allowed an extension only for 2014, HHS concludes it lacks statutory authority for a categorical 60-day automatic extension beyond the 90 days. The proposal questions whether §155.315(f)(3) good faith extensions conform with statute but treats them as appropriate ad hoc uses of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create annual household income DMI when attestation ≥100% FPL and IRS/SSA <100% (§155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require Exchanges to generate annual household income inconsistencies when: (1) the consumer attested to projected annual household income between 100% and 400% of the FPL; (2) the Exchange has IRS and SSA data indicating household income is below 100% of the FPL; (3) the Exchange has not assessed/determined Medicaid or CHIP eligibility; and (4) the attested projected income exceeds electronic data by a reasonable threshold established by the Exchange and approved by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: reinstate provisions vacated from 2019 because new enrollment/tax data and studies show evidence of intentional income inflation or assisted misreporting leading to improper APTC payments. Process: generate DMI per §155.315(f)(1)-(4); applicant has 90 days to resolve, may request extension in certain circumstances; if unresolved, Exchange redetermines eligibility, typically discontinuing APTC/CSR. Seeks comment on costs/benefits and calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable threshold for triggering DMI (minimum 10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed reasonable threshold for when an applicant's attested income 'exceeds the income reflected in the data available from electronic data sources' must not be less than 10% and can also include a threshold dollar amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS invites comments and data to help calibrate the threshold to maximize program integrity while minimizing unnecessary administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redetermination outcome when documentation is not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to provide documentation verifying their household income attestation in response to the DMI, the Exchange would redetermine the applicant's eligibility for APTC and CSRs based on available IRS data, which under this proposal would typically result in discontinuing APTC and CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adjustment and notification process would operate like other inconsistency adjustments laid out in §155.320(c)(3)(vi)(F) and (G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove exception allowing self-attestation when IRS tax data unavailable (§155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.320(c)(5), which currently requires Exchanges to accept an applicant's or enrollee's self-attestation of projected annual household income when the Exchange requests tax return data from the IRS but the IRS confirms there is no such tax return data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the proposal, this exception would be removed so that when IRS and other trusted data sources cannot resolve a DMI, applicants must submit documentary evidence or otherwise resolve the inconsistency with the data source (i.e., self-attestation alone would not suffice). Seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer burden and timeframe assumptions for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated burden: answering verification questions and submitting supporting documents would take consumers approximately 1 hour; 90-day period provided to resolve DMIs is considered sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS believes the 1-hour estimate is minimal relative to program integrity benefits, though consumers may require longer; extensions can be requested in certain circumstances. HHS seeks comment if burden estimates are inaccurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Federal Tax Information (FTI) in notice design
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct notices containing FTI must be sent by U.S. mail to the tax filer and must not be available online or through the Exchange call center; indirect notices must avoid disclosing FTI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design is intended to preserve FTI confidentiality while ensuring enrollees and tax filers receive required education and notice about filing/reconciling obligations and risk of losing APTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory imperative to verify with IRS and use additional trusted data sources where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1411–1414 of the ACA require HHS to submit applicant income information to the IRS for verification and to take further steps to verify income when inconsistent with IRS data, and section 1413 requires HHS to establish data matching arrangements with reliable third-party sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS asserts that this statutory framework compels requesting additional documentation when electronic data show income below the APTC threshold but the attestation is above it; HHS retains some discretion to use other data sources but may not avoid verification when necessary to protect program integrity.
